presentations.purpose: Compare categories; use horizontal bars for long labels.
presentations.unsuitable_for: A continuous trend over time — use line/area so order and spacing read correctly.

presentations.purpose: Compare categories with a lighter visual weight than full bars; single series only.
presentations.unsuitable_for: More than a handful of categories, or multiple series — the dot is easy to lose at high density and this type is single-series only.

presentations.purpose: Show the distance between exactly two measurements per category, e.g. before vs after or target vs actual; needs exactly two named series.
presentations.unsuitable_for: More than two measurements per category — use grouped bar for that.

presentations.purpose: Show ordered trends; use area to emphasize magnitude, step for values that change in discrete jumps rather than continuously.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Unordered categories — the line implies a sequence; use bar instead.

presentations.purpose: Show an uncertainty band or min/max range around a trend; each series needs a low and high value per x, not a single y.
presentations.unsuitable_for: A single point estimate at one x — use error_bar for one measurement’s uncertainty instead of a continuous band.

presentations.purpose: Show how multiple nonnegative series contribute to a total.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Series that can be negative — stacking assumes nonnegative contributions, or the running total stops meaning "total".

presentations.purpose: Show what share each nonnegative series contributes to a total, normalized to 100% so proportions are comparable across categories of different absolute size.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Comparing absolute totals across categories — normalizing to 100% hides them; use plain stacked_bar/stacked_area for that.

presentations.purpose: Show a trend at a glance with no axes or legend; for inline/compact scanning, not precise reading.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Anywhere a reader needs to read an exact value — axes and legend are hidden by design.

presentations.purpose: Show nonnegative parts of a whole, preferably 2–6 categories.
presentations.unsuitable_for: More than ~8 slices, or comparing across several pies — switch to bar, where length is easier to compare than angle.

presentations.purpose: Like pie, but each slice's radius scales with its value instead of just its angle, which emphasizes magnitude differences more strongly; nonnegative.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Precise value comparison — radius scaling exaggerates differences more than angle alone; use bar if accuracy matters more than impact.

presentations.purpose: Rank nonnegative categories by contribution and overlay cumulative percentage to find the vital few; single series only.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Multi-series comparison — it ranks exactly one measure, and the cumulative line only means something for one series.

presentations.purpose: Show a running total through a sequence of signed increases and decreases; single series where each point is a delta from the previous total, not an absolute value.
presentations.unsuitable_for: A static snapshot of values at one point in time — it specifically shows the running change from one period to the next.

presentations.purpose: Show a nonnegative quantity narrowing (funnel) or widening (pyramid) through ordered stages.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Data that doesn’t represent sequential stages of one process — use bar for unrelated nonnegative categories.

presentations.purpose: Show nonnegative parts of a whole as a 10x10 grid of unit squares, one block per percentage point; best for one proportion at a glance, not precise multi-way comparison.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Many categories or precise comparison — limited to the visual resolution of a 10x10 grid (100 squares).

presentations.purpose: Show a measurement plus its uncertainty range; like range_area but for a single point per x rather than a continuous band. Give low/high (and an explicit value if the drawn point is not their midpoint).
presentations.unsuitable_for: A continuous band across many x positions — use range_area for that.

presentations.purpose: Show relationships between two numeric measurements; use numeric x/y points.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Categorical x — needs genuinely numeric x/y pairs, or the relationship being shown isn’t real.

presentations.purpose: Like scatter, plus a third nonnegative magnitude encoded as point size (area-proportional, not radius-proportional, per perceptual accuracy); points need x, y and size.
presentations.unsuitable_for: A third dimension that isn’t a true magnitude — size implies quantity, not category; use color/category for that instead.

presentations.purpose: Scatter plus an overlaid ordinary-least-squares trend line fit to all points; the line is omitted only when every x value is identical.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Categorical or ordinal x, or fewer than two distinct x values — the regression needs genuinely numeric x with some spread.

presentations.purpose: Show the distribution of one sample of raw numeric observations, auto-binned into equal-width bins; single series only.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Comparing multiple samples — it’s exactly one sample binned; use box_plot or density for that.

presentations.purpose: Show the five-number summary (min, quartiles, max) of one or more named samples of raw observations, for comparing distributions across groups.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Seeing the actual shape of a distribution — it only shows five summary numbers; pair it with density for that.

presentations.purpose: Show a smoothed estimate of the distribution shape of one or more named samples, as a continuous curve rather than discrete bins.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Very small samples — a KDE on a handful of points can look smoother and more confident than the data justifies.

presentations.purpose: Show what fraction of a sample falls at or below each value, as a nondecreasing step curve from 0 to 1; good for comparing whole distributions without binning.
presentations.unsuitable_for: An intuitive "typical value" read for a general audience — use box_plot or density for that.

presentations.purpose: Show every raw observation of one or more named samples as points along one lane per sample, with no binning or smoothing.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Large samples — points overlap with no way to tell how many are stacked; use beeswarm or histogram instead.

presentations.purpose: Like strip_plot, but spreads overlapping points sideways within local density bins so individual observations stay visible rather than stacking on top of each other.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Very large samples — hundreds of points still crowd a fixed-width lane even after spreading.

presentations.purpose: Show pairwise scatter plots for 2-6 aligned numeric columns (each row is one observation across every column) in a grid; good for spotting which pairs of variables relate.
presentations.unsuitable_for: More than ~6 columns — cells shrink past legibility; pick the most relevant columns instead.

presentations.purpose: Show the pairwise Pearson correlation coefficient for 2-6 aligned numeric columns as a color-coded, labeled grid.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Understanding the shape of a relationship — it collapses each pair to one number; pair it with scatter_matrix for the shape.

presentations.purpose: Show each observation as a line crossing one axis per aligned numeric column (2-6), for spotting patterns across many dimensions at once.
presentations.unsuitable_for: More than a handful of columns or many overlapping rows — crossing lines become unreadable past that.

presentations.purpose: Show one or more named profiles scored across the same set of indicators (the x labels), one axis per indicator; a series missing an indicator counts as 0 there.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Indicators on very different scales without normalizing them first — the shape will mislead rather than inform.

presentations.purpose: Like bar, but arranged around a circle (angle = category, radius = value); good for cyclical categories like hours of day or months of year.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Precise value comparison — angular/radial position is harder to judge accurately than a linear bar’s length.

presentations.purpose: Show a single measurement against a min/max range (default 0-100), optionally with a target shown in the label; 1-6 named gauges per chart.
presentations.unsuitable_for: More than a handful of gauges at once, or a trend over time — it’s a single instantaneous reading, not a time series.

presentations.purpose: Show a measurement against a target and qualitative background bands (e.g. poor/satisfactory/good) within a min/max range; 1-6 named bullets per chart.
presentations.unsuitable_for: More than a handful of bullets at once — legibility drops fast past that.

presentations.purpose: Show one or more named values as a filled bar against a max (default 100); a lightweight progress/thermometer indicator, not a dial.
presentations.unsuitable_for: A trend over time, or a value whose meaningful exceeding of max matters — it’s a single snapshot against a ceiling.

presentations.purpose: Show a value for every combination of two independent categorical keys (e.g. a cohort/retention matrix) as a color-coded grid; single series of cells only.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Sparse data — mostly-empty cells waste the grid; consider bar or scatter instead.

presentations.purpose: Show one value per day as a color-coded GitHub-style calendar grid; reuses the plain {label, value} shape with label as an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).
presentations.unsuitable_for: More than roughly a year of days — cells become illegibly small past that.

presentations.purpose: Show open/high/low/close per period (e.g. trading day), optionally with a traded volume overlay on a second axis colored by up/down.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Data that isn’t genuinely OHLC over ordered periods — a plain price series belongs on a line chart instead.

presentations.purpose: Show percentage decline from the running peak of a value series over time; reuses the line/area data shape, always nonpositive by construction.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Values that already sum to 0 or alternate sign arbitrarily — built for a cumulative equity/price-style series with a meaningful running peak.

presentations.purpose: Show compounded growth from a series of periodic returns (e.g. 0.02 for +2%), not price levels; reuses the line/area data shape.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Price levels given directly — give periodic returns, not prices, or the compounding is computed on the wrong thing.

presentations.purpose: Show tasks as horizontal bars spanning low-high on a numeric timeline (not a calendar date axis), one row per task; a row with low === high draws a milestone marker instead, so a plain timeline of events is just every row being one. Up to 50 rows; group optionally colors rows together.
presentations.unsuitable_for: A calendar-dated schedule — the axis is a plain numeric timeline (e.g. days since start), not real dates.

presentations.purpose: Show a nested hierarchy (recursive {name, value?, children?} nodes; a leaf needs value, a branch sums its children) as nested rectangles (treemap) or nested rings (sunburst); several top-level nodes are fine.
presentations.unsuitable_for: Negative values, or more than a few levels deep — labels become illegible past that.

presentations.purpose: Show a nested hierarchy as a rooted node-link layout (dendrogram); exactly one top-level root, since a rooted layout cannot draw several trees at once.
presentations.unsuitable_for: More than one root, or a very deep/wide hierarchy — labels crowd fast.

presentations.purpose: Show weighted flow between stages as proportionally-sized ribbons; one combined {nodes, links} graph, every link needs a nonnegative value since it sizes the flow's width. A link's optional `type` gives flows of that relationship a stable, distinct color.
presentations.unsuitable_for: A true network with cycles or bidirectional flow — sankey assumes a left-to-right staged flow.

presentations.purpose: Show a node-link network (force-directed layout); one combined {nodes, links} graph, link value is optional and only affects line width, not required the way sankey needs it. A link's optional `type` (e.g. "dependency", "similarity") gets a stable color and an edge label distinguishing it from other relationship types between the same nodes; `directed: true` draws an arrowhead.
presentations.unsuitable_for: More than roughly 100 nodes — the force layout gets crowded and slow past that.

instructions: Use render_chart with computed values. Do not invent data. Use render_table for exact values and render_kpi_cards for headline numbers. No code, callbacks, remote URLs or executable specifications.

interactions.zoom_pan: Scroll/pinch to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to reset — built into every chart whose type is in INTERACTIVE_CHART_TYPES; nothing to request.
interactions.legend_toggle: Click a legend entry to show/hide that series — built into every multi-series chart; nothing to request.
interactions.reference_lines: Optional top-level reference_lines: [{value, label?}], up to 10, for chart types in INTERACTIVE_CHART_TYPES. Draws a dashed line across the value axis — a target or baseline to compare against, not data.
interactions.sort: Optional top-level sort: 'asc'|'desc', for chart types in SORTABLE_CHART_TYPES. Reorders by value; omit it and the input order is kept exactly as given.
interactions.export: mountChatChart(...) returns svg() and png() for exporting the rendered chart; both are host-side JS calls, not part of the JSON payload.
interactions.visual_style: Optional top-level visual_style, default 'flat'. 'outlined', 'glassmorphism' and 'skeuomorphism' rewrite a series' own fill and are restricted to FILL_SAFE_CHART_TYPES (fill is decorative there, not the data encoding); the other eight ('minimalism', 'material', 'neumorphism', 'claymorphism', 'editorial', 'technical', 'hand_drawn', 'brutalist') only touch chrome/border/shadow/typography and apply to every chart_type. 'glassmorphism' falls back to an opaque fill automatically under high_contrast, per the plan's 'high contrast takes precedence over ornament'.
interactions.drill_down_and_cross_filtering: Not available from this portable, read-only contract — it requires a host-side data query or document commit, which an agent cannot embed as code. The Generative BI document surface has its own selection/query-bound interaction model for this; the chat contract does not share it.
